chapters.title: Introduction
chapters.html:
Buying a first property in Quebec when you have just arrived involves particular challenges: building local credit, understanding a different system, and navigating vocabulary and rules specific to the province. Well accompanied, it is completely accessible.

This guide provides guidelines for newcomers: credit and financing, Quebec specificities, and steps to prepare.

Informative content. Each chapter ends with a lined “My Notes” page.

Buying a first property in Quebec as a newcomer involves particular challenges: building local credit, understanding a different system, learning your own vocabulary. Well accompanied, it is completely accessible. This guide gives the key points.

Informative content: validate your situation with the professionals concerned.

chapters.title: Building your credit and financing file
chapters.objective: Make yourself financeable in the local system.
chapters.html:
Make yourself financeable in the local system.

Lenders look at your Canadian credit, your income and your stability. A local credit history can take time to build.

  • Start building credit early (card, on-time payments).
  • Gather proof of income and employment.
  • Explore the programs for newcomers, under special conditions.

The more solid and documented your file is, the simpler and more advantageous the financing will be.

Lenders look at your Canadian credit, your income and your stability. A local history takes time to build: open a card when you arrive and pay it in full each month. Some programs for newcomers offer adapted conditions, via a mortgage broker.

Emilie's advice

Open a credit card upon arrival and pay it in full each month. Building a Canadian history takes months: start well before you think about buying.

chapters.title: Understanding Quebec specificities
chapters.objective: Learn the rules of the local game.
chapters.html:
Learn the rules of the local game.

The Quebec system has its particularities, often different from what exists elsewhere:

  • Role of notary (mandatory) and broker (supervised by the OACIQ).
  • Welcome tax, municipal and school taxes.
  • Co-ownership divides/undivides, leases and rental rules if plex.
  • Particularities of the building (clay soils, French drain, heating, winter).

Understanding them in advance avoids many costly surprises.

The Quebec system has its particularities: mandatory notary, broker supervised by the OACIQ, welcome tax, divided/undivided co-ownership, leases if plex, and a building specific to the climate (clay soils, French drain, winter). Learning the local vocabulary already means avoiding half of the mistakes.

Emilie's advice

Take the time to learn the local vocabulary: “welcome tax”, “certificate of location”, “conditions of the promise to purchase”. Understanding words already means avoiding half of the mistakes.

chapters.title: Prepare yourself and surround yourself well
chapters.html:
Move forward with confidence.

As any first buyer, prepare the foundations:

  • Establish a budget realistic.
  • Obtain a pre-approval mortgage.
  • Define your criteria and your sectors.

As a bonus, surround yourself with professionals who understand your journey (broker, mortgage broker, notary). Learning the local market before you buy is an investment that pays off.

As any first buyer, lay the foundations: realistic budget, pre-approval, criteria and sectors. As a bonus, surround yourself with professionals used to supporting newcomers - a good broker will explain not only the houses, but the entire system around them.

Emilie's advice

Choose professionals used to supporting newcomers. A good broker will explain not only the houses, but the whole system around them - it's invaluable.

chapters.html:

A mortgage broker can help you put everything together in the most advantageous way.

The minimum down payment depends on the price; below 20%, loan insurance is added. Save early, check your eligibility for assistance programs, and know that a family donation is accepted with a donation letter. A mortgage broker helps you put everything together advantageously.

Emilie's advice

Find out about programs for first-time buyers and newcomers: some offer favorable conditions. A mortgage broker knows what you are entitled to.

chapters.title: From research to taking possession
chapters.objective: Follow the route step by step.
chapters.html:
Follow the route step by step.

Once financed and well supported, the purchasing process follows a clear logic:

  1. Visit according to your criteria and sectors.
  2. Make a promise to purchase with the right conditions (financing, inspection).
  3. Carry out theinspection and lift the conditions.
  4. Sign with the notary and take possession.

At each stage, ask your questions: no one expects a newcomer to already know the entire system.

The route follows a clear logic: visit according to your criteria, make a promise to purchase with the right conditions (financing, inspection), lift the conditions after inspection, then sign with the notary. At each stage, ask your questions: no one expects a newcomer to already know everything.

Emilie's advice

Don't be afraid to ask “too many” questions. A good professional would rather answer your questions a thousand times than see you sign without understanding. This is your biggest purchase.

chapters.title: Action plan
chapters.html:
Your next steps, concretely.

This week

  1. Start or consolidate my Canadian credit.
  2. Gather my proof of income and employment.

Within 30 days

  1. Meet a mortgage broker (newcomer programs).
  2. Inform me about Quebec specificities.

Then

  1. Obtain pre-approval and launch my search with Emilie.

To prepare myself

  1. Build my Canadian credit and gather my proof of income.
  2. Meet with a mortgage broker (newcomer programs) and obtain pre-approval.
